Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.config

Class ServerEyeConfigs

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.config.ServerEyeConfigs
public final class ServerEyeConfigs extends Object
Server-authoritative store of eye geometry configs, loaded from datapacks by EyeConfigReloadListener. The server uses this to gate hasGooglyEyes (see ServerServices.onLivingEntityLoaded(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity)) and to build the sync payload sent to clients.

Kept separate from ClientEyeConfigs so the integrated server and client don't share one static map in single-player. Installed maps are immutable snapshots; their mutable model values are owned by this store and must be treated as read-only after installation.

  • Field Details

    • ENDER_DRAGON

      public static final net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation ENDER_DRAGON
      Hard-excluded from googly eyes: the ender dragon's renderer bypasses the LivingEntityRenderer family entirely (no eye layer can attach) and its model has no walkable part tree, so eyes can never render on it. EyeConfigReloadListener refuses datapack configs for it and /sg spawnall skips it.

    • canEverWearEyes

      public static boolean canEverWearEyes(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity living)
      Whether this entity can wear eyes at any life stage (baby or adult). Used by the at-spawn roll (ServerServices.onLivingEntityLoaded(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity)): that decision is stored for life, so a baby that only has an adult config must still be allowed to roll — otherwise it stores hasGooglyEyes=false and never re-rolls, locking it out of eyes forever even after it grows up. The client swaps in the age-appropriate geometry as the mob ages.

    • isEligible

      public static boolean isEligible(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity living)
      Whether this entity can wear eyes right now, at its current age: it has an age-appropriate config that is enabled and has at least one head. Used by the slimy eye (SlimyEyeItem), which should only apply to targets the eyes would visibly appear on immediately. Players have a definition (player.json) and so are eligible; only an unconfigured entity is not.

    • replaceAll

      public static void replaceAll(Map<net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation,EyeConfigModel.RuntimeConfigSet> next)
      Force-install a snapshot and discard its content signature. This is the unconditional replacement path used by tests; normal datapack reload uses replaceIfChanged(java.util.Map<net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation, com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.config.EyeConfigModel.RuntimeConfigSet>, java.lang.String).

    • replaceIfChanged

      public static boolean replaceIfChanged(Map<net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation,EyeConfigModel.RuntimeConfigSet> next, String nextSignature)
      Datapack-reload entry point: swap in the resolved set only when nextSignature (a canonical serialization of next, computed by the reload listener) differs from the installed set's. A /reload triggered for an unrelated datapack thus stops re-fanning the whole eye-config snapshot to every online player. Returns whether a swap happened.

    • onServerStopping

      public static void onServerStopping()
      Drop the content signature so the first reload of the next world always resynchronizes.
